title: Admit the actual weak meter without treating a norm as probability
statement: The main reported-plus parity matrix is [[1-q,gamma],[gamma,q]], gamma=exp(-2N)/2. Physical positivity gamma^2<=q(1-q) gives e=q+gamma^2/q and p=1-e. Explicit bad Kraus operators have coefficients (gamma/sqrt(q),sqrt(q)) on the two parity projectors, reversed for the other report; their summed KdagK is e*I. Thus M0=p*P+e*B is an EXACT input-independent CP mixture, with the largest uniform ideal weight in this form. Including the physical auxiliary channel gives M=p(1-pZ)*P+p*pZ*Ad_Z2*P+e*Lambda*B and e_total=e+pZ-e*pZ. The optimized values are e=.00100126858272, pZ=.000307090843994 and e_total=.00130805194630. Every residual Kraus operator is in Alg(Z1,Z2); the actual 4x4 Gram subtraction retains the auxiliary phase. Main half-diamond distance is sqrt(q^2+gamma^2), with full-instrument half-distance <=pZ+that quantity. A norm is not the CP fault probability. Independent location mixtures require earned vacuum renewal and independent admitted noise; thermal input, X/T1 faults, drift and shared memory are not included automatically.
